findings.title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is now an uninstantiable abstract class registered as detector_handler
findings.body: This change replaces `DetectorHandler` with `StatefulDetectorHandler` and removes the previously-present `def evaluate(...)` placeholder that returned `[]`. `StatefulDetectorHandler` declares four new abstract methods (`counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, `build_occurrence_and_event_data`), and `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` implements none of them. The class is therefore abstract. However, it is still referenced from `MetricAlertFire.detector_handler = MetricAlertDetectorHandler`, so any time `Detector.detector_handler` is accessed for a Detector with type `"metric_alert_fire"` (which `process_detectors` does unconditionally), `MetricAlertDetectorHandler(detector)` raises `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class MetricAlertDetectorHandler with abstract methods ...`. This aborts the entire `process_detectors` loop, preventing any further detectors in the list from being processed. Previously the class was concrete (it had a `def evaluate` that returned `[]`), so this is a regression. To fix, either implement the four abstract methods (with sensible stubs/raises-NotImplementedError where appropriate, but the class must still be concrete), or revert to `DetectorHandler` until the abstraction is actually built.

findings.title: build_occurrence_and_event_data exceptions leave state inconsistent (dedupe already bumped)
findings.body: In `evaluate_group_key_value`, `self.enqueue_dedupe_update(group_key, dedupe_value)` is called (line 265) before any later logic. Once `state_data.status != new_status`, the code reaches the new `else: result, event_data = self.build_occurrence_and_event_data(...)` branch. If that subclass hook raises (network failure, invalid `value` for the detector type, missing config, etc.), the function propagates the exception out of `evaluate_group_key_value`, the dict result is never produced, but the previously-enqueued `dedupe_updates[group_key]` and `state_updates[group_key]` still get committed by `handler.commit_state_updates()` after `process_detectors` catches the failure. On retry of the same data packet, `dedupe_value <= state_data.dedupe_value` will be true, so the data packet is permanently skipped and the issue is never produced. There is no try/except around `build_occurrence_and_event_data`, and no rollback of the enqueued dedupe/state update on failure. Either swallow and log errors (mirroring the `skipping_invalid_condition_group` branch), or roll back the dedupe/state enqueue when building the occurrence fails.

findings.title: build_occurrence_and_event_data called with PriorityLevel(new_status) but type was DetectorPriorityLevel
findings.body: The new call is `self.build_occurrence_and_event_data(group_key, value, PriorityLevel(new_status))`. `new_status` is a `DetectorPriorityLevel` (an IntEnum defined in `sentry.workflow_engine.types`), not a `PriorityLevel`. Passing one enum's integer value to the other enum's constructor relies on the underlying integer values matching, which is true today but is a fragile coupling between two enums in different modules. If `PriorityLevel` and `DetectorPriorityLevel` ever drift (e.g., one gains a new level the other doesn't), this will raise `ValueError: ... is not a valid PriorityLevel`. Either convert via the enum's `.value`/`.name` mapping explicitly, or document and assert the invariant.

findings.title: test_state_results_multi_group passes wrong value for group_2 to build_mock_occurrence_and_event
findings.body: The test packet is `{"dedupe": 2, "group_vals": {"group_1": 6, "group_2": 10}}`, but the assertion builds the expected occurrence with `build_mock_occurrence_and_event(detector.detector_handler, "group_2", 6, PriorityLevel.HIGH)` — i.e., value 6 instead of 10. The mock currently ignores `value`, so the test passes, but as soon as a future change to `build_mock_occurrence_and_event` actually uses `value` (e.g., to embed it in evidence_data or the subtitle), the test will start asserting against a value the production code path will never produce, masking real regressions. Use the actual packet value (10) for group_2.

findings.title: DetectorHandler.evaluate return type contract break not documented for third-party subclasses
findings.body: The abstract `DetectorHandler.evaluate` signature changed from `list[DetectorEvaluationResult]` to `dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]`, and all in-repo subclasses were updated. The PR description mentions this, but any out-of-tree subclass of `DetectorHandler` (e.g., downstream open-source detectors) will silently start returning the wrong shape and either crash at iteration (`.values()` on a list raises AttributeError) or behave incorrectly when keys collide. Consider a deprecation period that accepts both shapes (e.g., coerce to dict internally) or a clearer changelog note in the docstring so subclass authors are explicitly warned.
